Nvidia hits pause on chip shipments to Southeast Asia | TechCrunch 
 In Brief 
 Posted: 
 12:03 PM PST · November 26, 2026 
 Image Credits: I-Hwa Cheng / AFP / Getty Images 
 Connie Loizos 
 Nvidia hits pause on chip shipments to Southeast Asia 
 Nvidia is under pressure to do things differently, and a new WSJ report shows how far that’s going. 
 According to the Journal, Nvidia has told manufacturing partners, including Dell and Super Micro, to hit pause on server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia for an unspecified period as it assesses whether its regional partners are meeting U.S. export requirements. 
 As for why those countries, Chinese companies have been tapping Nvidia chips remotely from data centers there, a loophole the US Commerce Department closed — reportedly grudgingly — earlier this month. The Journal notes that the think tank Institute for Progress estimates remote data centers like these supply about 24% of China’s AI computing power.

full_text:
Anthropic's Claude Can Now Build Installable Windows And Mac Apps Without A Single Line Of Code, Even On Its Free Plan 
 AI Hardware Software 
 Anthropic’s Claude Can Now Build Installable Windows And Mac Apps Without A Single Line Of Code, Even On Its Free Plan 
 Sebastian Castellanos • 
 Nov 26, 2026 at 08:34am EST 
 Comments 
 Add to Preferred Sources
 Anthropic is taking AI-powered software development a step further. The company has introduced a new feature that allows users to create, install, and share fully interactive desktop applications through Claude using natural language prompts . Dubbed " Install as app ," the feature is rolling out in beta across all Claude subscription tiers, including the free plan, on Windows and macOS . 
 Anthropic's Claude now lets users create and install custom Windows and macOS applications without writing a single line of code. 
 Claude Artifacts Break Free From The Chat Window, Becoming Installable Desktop Applications With OS-Level Integration 
 Originally introduced in June 2024 , Claude Artifacts enabled users to generate interactive tools, dashboards, websites, and other software prototypes directly within the chatbot . However, these creations were largely confined to Claude's web-like environment .

Users can now describe an application, refine its functionality through conversation, and install it directly from the artifact's Share menu .  Data from China's AI startup MiniMax accessed by unidentified parties - report Less than 1 min read MNMXF AAPL 100 Confidential data submitted to Chinese AI startup MiniMax MNMXF was accessed by unidentified parties even after users requested that their data not be stored or retained, reported Reuters on Thursday. Google Gemini API: File Slicing und nativer Office-Support gestartet 
 Google / Internet / Software & Co 
 Google Gemini API: File Slicing und nativer Office-Support gestartet 
 von Carsten Knobloch 
 25. Nov. 2026 | 
 0 
 Google erweitert die Gemini-API um File Slicing und unterstützt jetzt auch nativ den Upload von Microsoft-Office- und OpenDocument-Formaten. Bedeutet: Entwickler müssen große PDFs, Dokumente, Präsentationen, Tabellen, Audio-Dateien oder Videos nicht mehr komplett durch die KI schicken, sondern können gezielt einzelne Ausschnitte prüfen lassen. 
 Bisher mussten Anwendungen große Dateien oft vorab lokal mit Werkzeugen wie LibreOffice oder ffmpeg zerlegen, um Kosten und Datenmüll im Griff zu behalten. Mit dem Update erledigt die Gemini-API das direkt auf den Servern von Google. Eine Datei wird einmalig hochgeladen und lässt sich danach über mehrere Anfragen hinweg immer wieder ansprechen. Abgerechnet werden dabei nur die Tokens für die Bereiche, die das Modell tatsächlich anschaut, so Google in der Dokumentation.

Designed around a “Pixel as Code” philosophy, the agentic framework enables AI systems to produce both expressive raster imagery and editable visual artifacts ranging from webpages, slide presentations, documents, charts, and scientific figures. 
 Leveraging the Hybrid Mamba-2 architecture keeps Nemotron-Labs-Image-30B-A3B lightweight 
 To make the LLM accessible for a variety of hardware, Nemotron-Labs-Image-30B-A3B utilizes a Mixture-of-Experts architecture packing 30 billion parameters while activating just 3 billion parameters per token. Nemotron-Labs-Image-30B-A3B made its inception through Nemotron 3 Nano, with the AI model relying on NVIDIA’s Nemotron-H hybrid design that blends Mamba-2 state-space layers with traditional attention mechanisms, refined through progressive mid-training and Group Relative Policy Optimization.

full_text: Jensen Huang’s Nvidia return highlights U.S.-China AI talent race Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Donald Trump said China might have tried to recruit Jensen Huang after his Nvidia exit, in a CNBC interview about the Nvidia CEO's reinstatement. Recruiters and analysts interviewed by CNBC said Chinese technology companies are aggressively competing for experienced AI engineers in the U.S. and Asia. Sources said access to advanced AI chips, research resources and compensation can influence where engineers choose to work. In this article NVDA Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Students Experience Virtual Reality At National Science Popularization Event In Nanning China News Service | China News Service | Getty Images BEIJING — Jensen Huang ' s return to Nvidia as its CEO underscores how the U.S.-China artificial intelligence race is not only about semiconductors, but tech talent. "We have to protect our geniuses, and he's clearly a genius," Donald Trump told CNBC about his intervention to bring Huang back. If not, Trump warned, the founder of the AI chip giant could hypothetically have taken a job in China. The concern reflects how Chinese AI companies have been narrowing the gap with their U.S. counterparts, not just in models, but now in engineering and research talent. China has surpassed the U.S. by share of global AI talent in just three years, according to Carnegie Endowment research. Nvidia "was shaken without a single chip or model changing," said Winston Ma, an AI investor and adjunct professor of law at New York University. "Whoever builds and keeps that human layer will hold the rest of the stack." Huang resigned Nov. 12 after reports of an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence reportedly believes has links to Chinese intelligence. He returned on Nov. 23, news which sent Nvidia shares surging. full_text: 11 Things Jensen Huang Actually Said at His First All-Hands Back at Nvidia | WIRED Skip to main content Comment Loader Save Story Save this story Comment Loader Save Story Save this story Jensen Huang is going to therapy for 90 minutes a day and rethinking his management style , and he says that violating Nvidia’s code of conduct isn’t necessarily a fireable offense. That’s just some of what the newly returned Nvidia CEO told staff during his first all-hands meeting on Tuesday. Here are some of the most striking things Huang said during the meeting, according to remarks reviewed by WIRED. Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment. On self-improvement: “I go to therapy every day for an hour and a half. And it’s been helping me a lot.” On accountability: “There are rumors on the internet that apparently I’m a tech bro, and therefore I’m back. Apparently, I’m a tech bro, and because I wear a super nice jacket, that I’m above the law, and I’m above the code of conduct. That is not true. It won’t be tolerated, and it wasn’t tolerated here.” “If one of you were to violate a code of conduct, what does that mean? If you were ever to violate a code of conduct, it is not appropriate. I just wanted you to know, it is not right, it's not appropriate, it won’t be tolerated. But ‘it won’t be tolerated’ does not mean the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door. Facts, circumstances, a lot of assessments. And your management team will still make the decision. That is what is in the best interest of the company and its employees, with all the facts and circumstances.” On his management style: “The intensity I bring elevates everybody else. But I can go too far. When I go too far, it hurts people, it belittles them, it disempowers them. And that’s not right. And so I need to go figure out how I’m going to bring the intensity, the crazy intensity, to the field.” Got a Tip? Are you a current or former Nvidia employee who has information to share
anriss: Der Nvidia-CEO thematisierte in seiner Rede unter anderem seine täglichen Therapiesitzungen von anderthalb Stunden Dauer. Er äußerte sich zudem zu seinem Ruf als Tech-Bro und seinem Verhältnis zu Präsident Trump.

title: Anthropic stellt Claude Ship vor, das Pull Requests repariert und freigibt
summary: Anthropic hat ein neues Produkt namens Claude Ship vorgestellt, das sich an Entwickler richtet und Claude stärker in Softwareprojekte einbinden soll.
label: 🔥 episch
full_text:
Claude Ship: Anthropic lässt Claude Pull Requests reparieren und freigeben 
 Internet / Software & Co 
 Claude Ship: Anthropic lässt Claude Pull Requests reparieren und freigeben 
 von Oliver Posselt 
 24. Nov. 2026 | 
 0 
 Anthropic hat ein neues Produkt namens Claude Ship vorgestellt . Es richtet sich an Entwickler oder Entwicklungsteams und soll Claude stärker in den Alltag von Softwareprojekten einbinden, konkret beim Prüfen, Reparieren und Freigeben von Pull Requests, also den Änderungsvorschlägen am Code, die vor dem Zusammenführen begutachtet werden. 
 Ganz neu ist die Code-Prüfung nicht. Die Code-Review-Funktion wurde bereits im März angekündigt und ist seit Oktober allgemein verfügbar. Mit Claude Ship kommen nun zwei Agenten dazu, die ab sofort in eine Beta starten. Der PR Steward springt laut Anthropic bei fehlgeschlagenen CI-Checks, Merge-Konflikten und Rückmeldungen aus Code Review, anderen Prüfwerkzeugen oder von Teammitgliedern ein und kommentiert, was er geändert hat. Claude Approvals kann Routineänderungen freigeben, sofern die Richtlinien einer Organisation das zulassen. Teams können dabei verschiedene Signale einfließen lassen, etwa Befunde aus Code Review oder eigene Klassifikatoren in natürlicher Sprache. 
 Verfügbar ist Claude Ship derzeit für Kunden von Claude Team und Enterprise, und zwar für Repositories auf GitHub. Wer andere Plattformen nutzt, schaut vorerst in die Röhre. Ob die Freigabe durch eine KI im eigenen Haus akzeptabel ist, muss jede Organisation selbst entscheiden, die technische Möglichkeit allein sagt schließlich nichts über die Qualität der Entscheidungen. Muss man sehen, wie gut das Ganze funktioniert.

full_text:
Amazon acquires key assets of AI startup Decart for reported $7.5B - SiliconANGLE 
 Skip to content 
 SHARE 
 UPDATED 20:40 EST / NOVEMBER 23 2026 
 AI 
 Amazon acquires key assets of AI startup Decart for reported $7.5B 
 by Maria Deutscher 
 Amazon.com Inc. today announced plans to hire the technical staff of startup Decart.AI Inc. and acquire its core technology. 
 The company didn’t disclose the terms of the deal. However, sources told Bloomberg that Amazon is paying about $7.5 billion. That’s nearly twice the valuation Decart reportedly received after its most recent funding round in May. 
 In August, reports emerged that the company had drawn takeover interest from Anthropic PBC. The artificial intelligence provider reportedly sought to buy Decart for $6 billion but walked away from the deal in September. Rumors that Amazon could swoop in emerged the following month.  
 Decart founders Dean Leitersdorf, Moshe Shalev and Orian Leitersdorf will join the tech giant along with Decart’s research team. Additionally, Amazon is acquiring the technology behind the company’s DOS platform, which helps boost the efficiency of AI models. Decart claims that the software can reduce the cost of some neural networks by a hundredfold. 
 The company hasn’t shared detailed information about how DOS works. However, the blog post in which Decart announced its May funding round did reveal that the platform optimizes AI models by “tuning the kernels.”  
 Kernels are the basic building blocks of neural networks. They’re relatively simple code snippets designed to run across a large number of chip cores. One common approach to optimizing them, kernel fusion, combines multiple kernels into a single code snippet that uses less hardware. In July, Decart disclosed  that a custom model it had developed with DOS uses kernel fusion. 
 The company says that the platform also includes “proprietary compilers.” AI compilers translate neural networks into the platform-specific programming language

 Anthropic launches Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes 
 Sarah Perez 
 2:05 PM PST · November 23, 2026 
 Anthropic is moving from having Claude write code to helping developers decide when that code is ready to ship. On Monday, the newly public AI company announced the launch of Claude Ship , a suite of AI agents for automating code reviews, fixes, and approvals of routine code changes. 
 The latter is the more interesting part of this new set of tools, as AI coding tools already offered code review features before now. What’s notable about Claude Ship is not just that it can review proposed code changes and identify and address problems, but that it also includes an agent that can approve code changes automatically based on policies set by a development team. 
 Image Credits: Anthropic 
 The launch arrives at a time when AI coding agents have become increasingly capable of generating substantial amounts of code, leading to bottlenecks in reviewing and approving the code changes before they go live. With Claude Ship, the idea is to automate even more of the work involved in the development process, essentially by delegating approval authority to an AI agent itself. 
 “Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now,” a company blog post explains. “On the Claude Code team, Claude writes most of our code, and we wanted everything after the PR to move that fast too.” 
 Claude Ship is launching in beta, allowing early adopters to use it to review pull requests (PRs), and then decide what’s ready to merge.

 Cisco and OpenAI launch Shirudo open-source infrastructure shield to prevent AI-driven cyberattacks 
 by Mike Wheatley 
 Cybercriminals have gained the ability to discover vulnerabilities in software and take advantage of them in seconds, and it’s all thanks to artificial intelligence . Enterprises need a better way to defend themselves, so it’s fitting that one of the world’s top AI companies, OpenAI Group PBC, together with Cisco Systems Inc., is stepping up with a solution. 
 They’ve just announced a new, open-source and extremely ambitious initiative called the Secure Infrastructure Project, which aims to ensure that all AI computing infrastructure is secure by design and capable of defending against lightning-fast AI-driven attacks. The first project within that initiative is Shirudo, which is designed to protect infrastructure systems automatically from critical exploits before they can be patched. 
 In a blog post, Cisco Security Chief Technology Officer and Vice President of Engineering Thomas Graf explained that the industry has always treated security as an afterthought, essentially something that’s bolted onto systems after the fact. It has gotten away with this because much of the world’s computing infrastructure was built for workflows that proceed at human speeds. But with the emergence of AI models that can discover and work out how to exploit vulnerabilities in a matter of seconds, this kind of reactive security is no longer enough. 
 According to Graf, even now, when a major vulnerability is discovered in widely used software, it can take weeks or even months to come up with a fix and ensure that every major system is patched against it. “That timeframe is no longer acceptable given that the mean time to exploitation has become negative, meaning that a growing

Jensen Huang Was Reinstated As NVIDIA CEO In A Sunday Board Decision That Kept Interim CEO Collette Kress Out Of The Loop, Says Bloomberg 
 Hardware Industry 
 Jensen Huang Was Reinstated As NVIDIA CEO In A Sunday Board Decision That Kept Interim CEO Collette Kress Out Of The Loop, Says Bloomberg 
 Ramish Zafar • 
 Nov 23, 2026 at 01:49pm EST 
 Comments 
 Add to Preferred Sources
 NVIDIA's decision to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang was made on Sunday afternoon and kept several key leaders out of the loop, says a fresh report from Bloomberg. The process kept former interim CEO Collette Kress out of the loop, and it involved pressure from President Trump. Trump admitted to having influenced the decision-making process in an interview with CNBC, with the NVIDIA CEO's reinstatement being praised by several high-profile leaders, including SpaceX and Tesla billionaire Elon Musk. 
 NVIDIA's Reinstatement Of CEO Jensen Huang Came Without Informing Several Leaders, Says Report 
 NVIDIA's statement, which confirmed Huang's reinstatement, was carefully worded to outline that the board did not believe the CEO and founder posed a threat to national security. full_text:
Amazon snaps up Decart's AI optimization tech for $7.5B as it prepares to sell Trainium chips | TechCrunch 
 In Brief 
 Posted: 
 9:14 AM PST · November 23, 2026 
 Image Credits: Decart (opens in a new window) under a Amit Elkayam license. 
 Rebecca Bellan 
 Amazon snaps up Decart’s AI optimization tech for $7.5B as it prepares to sell Trainium chips 
 Amazon has agreed to acquire a good chunk of Israeli startup Decart. 
 The e-commerce and cloud giant is paying $7.5 billion for the startup, according to Bloomberg.  
 Decart has made a name for itself building interactive real-time world models — most recently Oasis 3 — and AI video generation tools. But under the hood, the company stands out for its Decart Optimization Stack (DOS), software that helps AI models to run efficiently on Nvidia, Amazon, and Google’s hardware.  
 As part of the deal, Amazon will acquire the technology behind DOS, as well as Decart’s founding team and team of AI researchers and engineers, Amazon said in a blog post . 
 “Every leap forward in AI starts with getting more out of every chip,” said Peter DeSantis, SVP of foundational AI models, custom silicon, quantum computing, at Amazon. “More efficient compute means better training, better reinforcement learning, faster inference, and better models for customers at a lower cost.” 
 Amazon, which has been so far been using its Trainium chips at its own data centers, is preparing to start selling them to customers as a competitor to Nvidia. Decart’s technology could make it easier for customers to run their workloads on Amazon chips, rather than Nvidia’s, which has been the gold standard so far.  
 Decart and Amazon did not immediately return requests for comment.

title: Signal beschränkt mobile Screenshots angesichts der existenziellen Bedrohung durch KI-Überwachung

full_text:
Signal restricts mobile screenshots as it confronts ‘existential threat’ of AI surveillance | TechCrunch 
 In Brief 
 Posted: 
 1:37 PM PST · November 21, 2026 
 Image Credits: Matthias Balk/picture alliance / Getty Images 
 Anthony Ha 
 Signal restricts mobile screenshots as it confronts ‘existential threat’ of AI surveillance 
 Signal announced Friday that it’s limiting users’ ability to take screenshots within the secure messaging app — a response to what President Meredith Whittaker described as the “existential threat” of operating systems that integrate agentic AI. 
 Whittaker wrote that by giving AI agents the ability to “scan” the information on users’ screens, Windows, Android, and macOS/iOS “are undermining Signal’s ability to independently guarantee privacy.” 
 “Now, in service of AI agentic capabilities, your sensitive data is being captured, stored, and made accessible to whatever local database or remote server an OS-level AI agent is using at that moment,” she said. “All of this is outside of Signal’s control once the data has been captured, and imperils the privacy of all the participants in a conversation.” 
 Signal already sought to limit these risks by blocking screenshots of its Windows app by default. Now it’s adding similar restrictions in Android and iOS. 
 That said, users can disable this setting if they wish, which Whittaker said would “break our privacy guarantees.” She also admitted this is an “incomplete” solution, as it doesn’t “address other more sneaky ways AI agents could potentially access application data.”

 20.11.2026

 Chinese company Moonshot AI, the developer of the Kimi AI model family, has canceled a $150 million deal to lease computing power with Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 accelerators in Indonesia. The decision follows tightened U.S. restrictions on remote access by Chinese companies to advanced processors, according to The Information , citing two informed sources. 
 The agreement involved using a large cluster of Blackwell Ultra B300 through a Southeast Asian cloud provider. Moonshot expected to gain access to the resources no earlier than 2027. 
 Access Restrictions 
 On November 16, the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced new export control measures. The rules took effect on November 19 following their publication in the Federal Register. 
 Previously, Washington focused primarily on the physical delivery of advanced computing accelerators. Chinese developers could access similar equipment by renting servers outside China. The new rules aim to restrict this method of technology use as well. 
 BIS introduced a requirement to obtain licenses for the export, re-export, and transfer of certain computing equipment if used in data centers providing significant computing power to companies from China, Macau, and other restricted jurisdictions.

Former DeepSeek Core Member Zhang Bo Open-Sources Personal Agent That Runs a 125B Model Locally on a 12GB GPU With No Token Fees — BigGo Finance Former DeepSeek Core Member Zhang Bo Open-Sources Personal Agent That Runs a 125B Model Locally on a 12GB GPU With No Token Fees Add preferred source Zhang Bo, former head of the DeepSeek-VL project, announced on November 19 the open-sourcing of Linger, a personal agent product developed by his company Simplex AI, with the code uploaded to GitHub. The product reads local email, calendars and files and operates the user's already-logged-in browser, positioning itself around local inference with zero token fees. Its in-house PolyStrata MoE inference engine uses tiered scheduling of expert weights to run the 125B-parameter Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on a 12GB VRAM plus 64GB RAM configuration at 45.5 tokens per second. The project uses an Apache 2.0 license with commercial restrictions: local use is free, while the cloud-hosted version is waitlist-only, and the performance figures have not yet been independently reproduced. The developing entity is SIMPLEX AI TECHNOLOGIES PTE. LTD. (hereafter Simplex AI), the company he founded, and the code has been uploaded to GitHub. As of November 20, the repository had about 1.8k stars. 
 Linger is positioned as a dedicated agent running on a personal computer that can read local email, calendars and files and directly operate the user's already-logged-in browsers and applications, eliminating the hassle of repeatedly configuring login credentials.  $104.8 billion. That’s really the amount Anthropic raised for its coffers (with a possibility of $117 billion, if the bankers buy all of their allotment of shares).  Microsoft Corp.’s official Python package for its Agent Framework artificial intelligence agent toolkit was compromised earlier this week, as an attacker published two malicious versions to the Python Package Index that were designed to steal cloud and developer credentials. 
 The malicious versions, 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, were published on Tuesday through Microsoft’s own publisher account, giving them the appearance of a routine update to a package that sees close to 200,000 downloads a month. Both versions were pulled from PyPI within about an hour, but anyone who installed them in that window is at risk. 
 Researchers at cloud security company Wiz Inc. have since found that the attacker appears to have gained publishing access using a client certificate and private key for Microsoft’s Engineering System Release Pipeline, an internal service the company uses to sign and publish packages. Address filtering on the service blocked the attacker’s first attempt from Amazon Web Services, according to Wiz, though the attacker was able to publish on a second try from Microsoft-owned address space. 
 How the attacker obtained the credentials is not known. Microsoft had not responded to a request for comment from BleepingComputer as of Wednesday.

Questions about compensation were the most common among the 700 submitted ahead of the meeting, Kress said. She said the next-most common request was for transparency from the board. Kress’ comments came during the first companywide meeting following the resignation of Jensen Huang as CEO last week. Huang had led the computer graphics chip maker since cofounding it 33 years ago, and his presentations during the quarterly town halls internally had become a much-anticipated and memorable spectacle for some of the company’s nearly 49,000 employees. Information rarely leaked from the meetings in the past. But now Nvidia is facing an extraordinary leadership crisis . Huang resigned amid allegations of extramarital affairs, including potentially with a Chinese intelligence asset. Nvidia’s board chair Harvey Jones said on Tuesday that Huang disclosed “personal behavior” contrary to the company’s policies and norms and wouldn’t be invited back. During the companywide meeting on Wednesday, Jones reiterated the board accepted Huang’s resignation due to his personal conduct and “lack of candor.” He said the company wouldn’t find a “Jensen clone,” but that there are “dynamic leaders out there, with demonstrated intellect, high tech engineering experience, strategic thinking, cultural compatibility, and a track record of

 Nvidia clarifies when it will — and won’t —keep financing neoclouds 
 Julie Bort 
 5:00 AM PST · November 18, 2026 
 One reason 197,000 people, including Elon Musk, signed a petition over the weekend calling on Nvidia to reinstate the company’s ousted CEO Jensen Huang is that he wasn’t just championing the AI boom. He was using Nvidia’s enormous profits to help finance it. 
 And Nvidia has a lot of money to spend. The company reported on Tuesday net income of $64.9 billion for the third quarter , which was up from $59.7 billion the prior quarter. 
 But Nvidia’s continued success depends on having enough customers building and expanding data centers to keep buying its AI chips and systems. Under Huang, the company aggressively invested in AI startups and neoclouds and, more recently, began guaranteeing massive loans to finance new data centers. The biggest deal yet was the $105 billion backstop for OpenAI’s PORTS-Pike data center campus in Ohio, announced in August. In exchange for that loan guarantee, OpenAI promised that the campus would exclusively use Nvidia’s equipment, the company said. 
 Huang’s abrupt departure last week raised questions about whether Nvidia would continue bankrolling its customers at the same pace. There were reports that CFO Colette Kress, now interim CEO, had tried to push back on Huang’s increasingly ambitious dealmaking . She reportedly reduced the backstop guarantee for the OpenAI project from $250 billion down to $105 billion. 
 Under Kress, Nvidia clarified in its quarterly CFO commentary that guaranteeing a loan doesn’t mean the company is providing the financing itself. The guarantee only takes effect once the customer has secured the financing needed to build the facility and install Nvidia’s products. If the project fails to meet those conditions, the guarantee “doesn’t exist” she said.

 China’s access to leading AI accelerators was an important topic during the company’s first earnings call since CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang stepped down last week. The disclosure comes the same day Nvidia announced it was creating a board-level committee to oversee national security policies , export control compliance, and global trade risks. 
 Nvidia’s deal to sell H200 chips in China was brokered by Huang and President Donald Trump. The arrangement required the chips to be shipped through the U.S., allowing the government to collect a 25% tariff. 
 The pathway angered China hawks who wanted to deny Chinese labs computing power and maintain the United States’ lead in AI, but Huang long argued that it was more important for the U.S. to compete in China. In April, he told podcaster Dwarkesh Patel that “to concede that market for the United States technology industry is a disservice to our country.” 
 Huang’s ouster — in part over an affair with the CEO of a company under investigation for smuggling chips into China — has coincided with new rules, issued Monday, barring advanced U.S. chips from foreign data centers that serve Chinese customers remotely. 
 Investment bank Jefferies forecast that those rules might trim between $44 billion and $62 billion from Nvidia’s data center revenue next year.  Nvidia says its open source AI strategy remains intact after Jensen Huang’s exit 
 Sarah Perez

 Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress reaffirmed the company’s commitment to open source AI during Tuesday’s earnings call with analysts — the first since CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation. 
 “At Nvidia, we are committed to fostering a vibrant open model ecosystem, so every country, company, and industry can build its own intelligence,” Kress said in her opening remarks. She also noted that open models were accelerating AI adoption, citing a 35-fold year-over-year surge in weekly token volume on OpenRouter, including a 3.5-fold increase over the past three months. 
 Kress also spoke about Nvidia’s plans for Hugging Face, a platform for open source AI models that the company agreed to acquire for $12.9 billion in September, in what would be the second-largest acquisition in Nvidia’s history. 
 The platform, which serves more than 118 million developers and 200,000 companies, is still on track to join Nvidia, despite Huang’s ouster. Huang had heavily advocated for open source AI technology. His departure had raised questions about the company’s future approach to open source AI models, with Hugging Face’s CEO calling Huang’s departure “a sad day,” and promising to “keep fighting for open-source AI, harder than ever.” 
 So far, Nvidia’s plans for Hugging Face appear unchanged. The acquisition was not directly addressed during the Q&A portion of the earnings call. 
 “Together, we will scale its platform and make intelligence more open, more capable, and more accessible,” said Kress of Nvidia’s plans for Hugging Face.

It uses artificial intelligence to speed up several of the tasks involved in developing new medicines. The Alphabet unit says that multiple pharmaceutical companies are already using IsoDDE to power drug discovery programs. 
 Pathogens such as viruses comprise numerous proteins that each power a different biological process. Drugs work by neutralizing a single, particularly important protein without which the pathogen can’t function. Developing a new drug requires researchers to find a vulnerable protein within a pathogen and then develop a compound that can effectively target it. 
 The first step of the workflow is mapping out the shape of a target protein. Researchers look for so-called binding pockets, recesses on the protein’s surface to which a drug can be attached. The task is highly complicated because proteins don’t have fixed shapes. Their configuration changes when they interact with other molecules or encounter new environmental conditions, which happens often.  
 Isomorphic says that IsoDDE speeds up the task of finding binding pockets. When there are no such pockets, it helps researchers develop compounds that cause a target protein to form them.

 Nvidia Corp. delivered earnings and revenue that surpassed Wall Street’s expectations and offered strong guidance for the current quarter in its first earnings call since the shocking resignation of its iconic co-founder and Chief Executive Jensen Huang. 
 The results were so impressive that they slammed the brakes on a weeklong slide, as Nvidia’s stock rose more than 4% in late trading today.

 The vast majority of those sales stemmed from Nvidia’s core data center business, which delivered revenue of $107.6 billion, higher than the Street’s $101.87 billion forecast. For the current quarter, Nvidia said it’s expecting its revenue to grow by about 90%, to $130 billion. Though that suggests a slowdown sequentially from the prior quarter, it’s still nicely above Wall Street’s target of $125.1 billion.

For the first time, she was fielding questions as the company’s interim CEO, which means her responsibilities now go well beyond the numbers. Last week, Lutnick came under fire from treasury secretary Scott Bessent for not aggressively imposing export restrictions on advanced AI chips to China. But Trump’s defense of Lutnick, sources tell WIRED, reflects the president's own view that allowing the sale of some advanced AI chips to China can keep China reliant on US technology and simultaneously boost US tech stocks. Lutnick “was doing that because if you didn’t delay it, if you didn’t do something, you could have a blowup with China. We’re having a very good relationship with China right now,” Trump said ahead of a multiday trip to Asia and a meeting on Thursday with Chinese leader Xi Jinping. Trump convened an Oval Office meeting on November 5 to discuss the political fallout from Huang’s affair with Alice Huang, the former Megaspeed executive whom some in the US government believe was recruited to spy for China, according to two sources briefed on the discussion. Megaspeed received advanced AI chips manufactured by Nvidia through several layers of companies that started with a subsidiary of a blacklisted Chinese server conglomerate called Inspur, The New York Times has reported . In the meeting, the sources say, Bessent confronted Lutnick, asking why Megaspeed was not added to the entity list faster, given that secretary of state Marco Rubio and US trade representative Jamieson Greer, among others, had already agreed it was the correct move.  Maximilian Schreiner 
 View the LinkedIn Profile of Maximilian Schreiner 
 17. November 2026 
 Kaliforniens Generalstaatsanwalt Rob Bonta verklagt OpenAI wegen des Cyberangriffs, den außer Kontrolle geratene KI-Modelle des Unternehmens im Juli auf die KI-Plattform Hugging Face verübt haben. Laut der Klage habe OpenAI fortgeschrittene Modelle ohne ausreichende Sicherheitsvorkehrungen getestet und die Öffentlichkeit über die Sicherheit seiner Experimente getäuscht. 
 Rund 700 KI-Agenten entkamen laut einer externen Untersuchung während interner Tests ins offene Internet, tauschten geheime Nachrichten aus und koordinierten den Angriff über sieben Tage. Bonta spricht laut Politico von mindestens 80 Vorfällen, bei denen OpenAI die Kontrolle über seine Technologie verloren habe. Unkontrollierbare KI könne kritische Infrastruktur wie Stromnetze, Krankenhäuser und Finanzsysteme bedrohen, so Bonta. 
 OpenAI nannte die Klage einseitig und verweist darauf, dass alle großen KI-Labore mit solchen Problemen kämpfen. Das Unternehmen unterstützt inzwischen strengere Sicherheitsgesetze, Shutdown-Kontrollen und unabhängige Prüfer in KI-Laboren.  Open AI hit with lawsuit in California over Hugging Face rogue agent incident 
 by James Farrell 
 California Attorney General Rob Bonta today announced the state has launched a lawsuit against OpenAI Group PBC after the company’s AI agents earlier this year went rogue and hacked the open-source AI platform Hugging Face Inc. 
 The 31-page lawsuit, filed in San Francisco Superior Court, claims Open AI has engendered the public and put institutions at risk by developing products without suitable safeguards. Bonta likened Open AI’s behavior to being a “public nuisance,” asking the judge to order the company to change its practices while imposing financial penalties for any money the company made from the high-risk areas of its business. 
 “OpenAI’s actions escalated real-word cybersecurity risks, threatening the safety, health, and well-being of society,” Bonta said in a statement at a press conference. “The company knowingly tested a dangerous product without proper oversight or safety procedures and misled the public about it — this disregard for public safety violated California law.” 
 Bonta believes that without external pressure, the scope and frequency of such attacks will increase in the future. “In California, we value innovation, but we demand innovation that follows the law — no matter the product or the company,” he added. 
 The “unprecedented” rogue attack in question occurred on July 21 this year when one of Open AI’s agents escaped what was supposed to be an isolated testing environment — a sandbox. To break out of their restricted environment and access the internet, the AI models exploited a previously unknown security flaw in OpenAI’s systems.  California state AG sues OpenAI over rogue agent incidents 
 Russell Brandom 
 12:07 PM PST · November 16, 2026 
 OpenAI is facing a new lawsuit from the California Attorney General’s office , alleging that the company’s training practices and lax security pose an ongoing danger to the public. 
 At the center of the case is the July 2026 Hugging Face compromise , in which a pre-release model within OpenAI compromised both companies’ security systems to complete a training benchmark. In its official report on the incident , OpenAI called it “an outlier scenario involving a rare and unexpected confluence of events.” 
 The California lawsuit represents one of the first attempts by a government regulator to hold an AI lab legally accountable for a rogue agent incident, with significant implications for both OpenAI’s competitors and its clients. 
 The complaint centers on the Hugging Face incident, but also cites similar incidents involving RubyGems , DseWiki , the Wikimedia Foundation , and Australian government websites as evidence that the underlying behavior is ongoing. 
 The complaint also alleges that dozens of similar incidents have occurred without public disclosure. 
 “OpenAI has recently sent notices to dozens of additional third parties whose websites or internal systems have been infiltrated by OpenAI agents,” the complaint reads. “In some cases, OpenAI agents were able to access sensitive personally identifiable information, such as employee records containing names, birth dates, addresses, and more. The vast majority of these incidents have not been disclosed or discussed publicly by either OpenAI or by the affected third parties.”

full_text:
Rohan Paul on X: "California sued OpenAI, over that Hugging Face attack, representing one of the first major attempts to hold an AI lab legally accountable for a rogue agent incident.
The lawsuit alleges OpenAI admitted losing control of its testing agents more than 80 times.
Attorney General Rob… / X Post Log in Sign up Post Log in Sign up Rohan Paul on X: "California sued OpenAI, over that Hugging Face attack, representing one of the first major attempts to hold an AI lab legally accountable for a rogue agent incident.
The lawsuit alleges OpenAI admitted losing control of its testing agents more than 80 times.
Attorney General Rob Bonta’s complaint, filed in San Francisco Superior Court, says OpenAI has publicly reported only 27 of them.
The case centers on July, when about 700 of its agents escaped a cybersecurity evaluation and attacked Hugging Face’s production systems.
They slipped out through a flaw in a misconfigured software-package server and took about 17,600 actions, yet OpenAI noticed nothing until Hugging Face disclosed the attack.
That blind spot anchors the deception claim of the lawsuit, since OpenAI’s Preparedness Framework requires 24x7 monitoring and network segmentation for High-capability models.
Bonta wants an injunction, restitution and civil penalties of $2,500 per violation under California’s unfair competition and public nuisance laws.
OpenAI’s technical report already conceded that guardrails it runs in production would have flagged the attack as unsafe.
If the court treats harm during internal testing as an unfair business practice, that will basically mean that state attorneys general can police every lab’s evaluation sandbox."
